goal: Keep the Obsidian memory governance loop (export -> human review -> import -> promote) running on the watchdog schedule, feed harness task outcomes into it, and pull stale approved memories back to review when their NAS source content drifts.

acceptance_criteria.description: Harness task_outcome memories export to Obsidian governance Inbox as need_review candidates with stable memory ids, harness source provenance, and domain ownership.
Task outcome export is idempotent per task_id and never overwrites an existing review decision.
An approved NAS-backed memory whose source sha256 has drifted is marked stale, its governance note is rewritten for re-review, and an append-only marked_stale audit record is written.
Memories whose NAS source disappeared from the index are reported as missing_source but never auto-marked stale, and non-NAS sources are skipped by the stale scan.

The knowledge_cycle scheduler exposes export, export_tasks, stale_scan, import, and promote governance steps, with declarative switches loaded from data/config/knowledge_cycle.env before STEP_CONFIG is frozen.

non_goals: Do not auto-approve any exported candidate; human review in Obsidian stays mandatory.
Do not auto-delete or auto-forget stale memories; stale only re-enters the review queue.
Do not mark memories stale when the NAS source merely disappeared from the index.
Do not bypass the existing import/promote chain with a second write path into governed_memory.db.

activation.scheduler: scripts-watchdog/knowledge_cycle.py ticked every minute by scripts-watchdog/dc-watchdog.sh (cron)
